newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Mideast and African port conditions - Lloyds.
newsitem.headline: Mideast and African port conditions - Lloyds.

text.p: Port conditions from Lloyds Shipping Intelligence Service --

ISRAEL, May 13 - No labour problem. Haifa - Six vessels discharging at berth (4 general cargo, 2 bulkers), 2 container vessels, 3 tankers. 1 Bulker waiting at anchorage to discharge, 3 container vessels, 1 tanker also anchored, 1 vessel under repair/dry-docked, 1 awaiting orders. 2 Vessels due with 1-2 days delay expected. Ashdod - 11 General cargo vessels discharging at berth, 2 bulkers loading at berth, 3 container vessels, 2 passenger vessels. 6 General cargo vessels waiting at anchor to discharge, 2 bulkers waiting to load, 1 container vessel also waiting. 2 Vessels awaiting orders, 2-3 days berthing delay expected. Eilat - One general cargo vessel discharging at berth. 4 Vessels loading at berth (1 general cargo, 1 bulker, 1 containers, 1 tanker), 1 passenger vessel, 1 bulker waiting at anchorage to load, 3 others also waiting (1 containers, 1 passenger vessel, 1 tanker). 1 Due.
JORDAN, May 10 - Aqaba - Four vessels loading at berth, 7 discharging at berth, 1 waiting at anchorage to load, 1 waiting to discharge.

MOZAMBIQUE, May 12 - Nacala - Port working normally. No restrictions on berthing and sailing during night time. Draft restrictions, 9.5 metres at general cargo berth and 14 metres at container berth. One tug available. Beira - General cargo berths - Working normally. Container terminal/other terminals - Working normally, 24 hour berthing/sailing for vessels up to 140 metres loa, some restrictions for larger vessels and subject to prior arrangements with port captain. Maximum draft for 24 hour navigation 7.5 metres. Two tugs available. General access channel - Two waverider buoys have been deployed in the approach channel as follows - Wmon1 19 deg. 66.0460 s 36 deg. 01.6698 e and Wmon2 - deg. 62.6370 s 34 deg. 62.6497 e. Each buoy has an approximate diameter of 1 metre, with flashing orange light with a flash frequency of five one-second flashes every 36 seconds.

Maputo - 24 Hour berthing/sailing for vessels up to 120 metres loa, some restrictions for larger vessels and subject to prior arrangements with port captain. All berths working normally and expected to remain so. Draft restriction in the channel is 9.0 metres less 0.5 metres (UKC) plus the rise of tide. Maximum draft for 24 hour navigation is 9 metres.
NAMIBIA, May 12 - Walvis Bay - Port working normally.

SOUTH AFRICA, May 12 - Richards Bay - General cargo berths - Working normally. Bulk import berths - Congested with delays of up to 8 days being experienced. Bulk export berths (minerals etc.) - Working normally. Bulk coal berths - Working normally with 2 vessels berthed, 1 due 12/5 and a further 17 due up to and including 19/5. No berthing delays at present. Durban - Container terminal - Delays of up to 96 hours can be expected whilst 2 new cranes are being positioned. Point/New pier/Maydon wharf berths - Working normally for general cargo vessels. Maize terminal (Maydon wharf 8) - Two vessels expected for May and 1 for June. Bunker supplies - Working normally, but delays of up to 8 hours presently experienced due to bunching of vessels. Dry-dock/floating dock - 50 Percent committed for May and 70 percent for June.

East London - General cargo/combi terminal/tanker berths - Busy, but no delays expected at this stage. Dry-dock - Open for bookings. Copper - 2,500 Metric tonnes moving out to the Far East. Tankers - 2 Expected weekly. Scrap steel - 8,500 Tonnes on hand. Port Elizabeth - Working normally, with 5 vessels in port. No delays expected on general, or tanker berths. Fruit berths - No delays at present, but berths will be fully occupied from 15-19/5. Ore berth - 1 Vessel berthed and a further 2 due this week. One vessel will experience C.A. 8 hours delay and the other 3 days delay. Ore plant working round the clock. Container berth - Berth under pressure and minor berthing delays expected. Two vessels in port. One gantry crane out of order and although the second gantry is working, the pulleys need replacement by 12/5. One vessel will experience between 10-20 hours delay.

Cape town - Breakbulk berths (general cargo) - Working normally, with vessels operating on arrival. Fruit berths - Fully occupied. Container terminal - Working normally, with vessels operating on arrival. Bunker berths - Vessels berthing and bunkering on arrival. Dry-docks and repair quays - Fully occupied. Booking is essential. Saldanha Bay - Port working normally.

TUNISIA, May 10 - Sousse - Two vessels in port, both discharging, of which 1 marble, 1 cotton. No delays, no vessels waiting. Sfax - Seven vessels in port operating of which 4 loading (1 bulk rock phosphate, 1 fish, 2 bulk tsp). 3 Discharging (1 general cargo, 1 bulk wheat, 1 bagged sugar). Tunis - One vessel discharging marble chips, 3 vessels awaiting instructions. Rades - 3 Ro-ro vessels. La Goulette - North side - 2 Vessels discharging (1 maize, 1 general cargo), 1 passenger vessel. South side - 1 Motor tanker, 1 vessel discharging grain, 1 loading zinc, 3 in roads. May 12 - Bizerte - Four vessels in port, all discharging, of which 1 timber, 1 wheat, 1 steel, 1 cpl. No berthing delays/congestion/strikes. Zarzis - No vessels, no berthing delays/congestion/strikes.

UNITED ARAB EMIRATES, May 4-10 - Dubai - No labour problems. 184 Vessels of which 75 containers, 10 general cargo, 2 general cargo/containers, 6 bulk carriers, 8 car carriers, 17 tankers, 4 naval vessels, 4 U.A.E. naval vessels, 1 livestock carrier, 3 bunkering/under repair/taking on stores etc., 5 dhows, 17 barges, 11 tugs, 17 supply boats, 1 chemical tanker, 2 lpg tankers, 1 passenger vessel. 3 Container vessels loading at berth, 6 vessels discharging at berth (5 general cargo, 1 tanker), 1 general cargo vessel bunkering. 11 Vessels under repair/laid-up (3 general cargo, 8 tankers), 39 due (25 containers, 9 general cargo, 5 tankers).

YEMEN, May 11 - Hodeidah - Eight vessels berthed of which 3 flour, 1 steel, 1 bulk wheat, 1 rice, 1 equipment, 1 general cargo. 2 Vessels anchored awaiting berths of which 1 flour, 1 frozen chicken. Berthing delays, general cargo (steel, timber, powder, etc.) 2-3 days, bagged cargoes (sugar, rice, wheat flour, etc.) 3-4 days, bulk wheat/corn 5-7 days, containers 1 day, reefers 36 hours. May 12 - Hodeidah - All berths occupied except No.8. Seven vessels berthed of which 3 flour, 1 containers, 1 wheat, 1 steel, 1 rice. 2 Vessels anchored of which 1 chicken, 1 flour. Berthing delays, general cargo up to 2 days, bagged cargoes up to 4 days, bulk cargoes up to 6 days, containers up to 1 day. Mokha - No vessels, no berthing delays.
